      <title>Fears grow that US will impose sanctions on ICJ judges ahead of Myanmar genocide ruling</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/us-sanctions-icj-judges-myanmar-genocide-ruling-israel-gaza-court</link>
      <description><p>A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza</p><p>Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize">Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay</a>, if the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/15/myanmar-rohingya-genocide-icj">court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide</a> against the Rohingya.</p><p>The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/us-sanctions-icj-judges-myanmar-genocide-ruling-israel-gaza-court">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans</link>
      <description><p>Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans</p><p>The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.</p><p>The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/mar/17/egypt-eu-deal-refugees-mediterranean">promised by Ursula von der Leyen</a>, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda</link>
      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/how-ukraine-struck-kerch-bridge-symbol-vladimir-putin-rule</link>
      <description><p>With the SpaceX satellite system faltering, Ukraine’s military launched a surprise, multi-pronged attack to take down vital bridge to Crimea</p><p>At 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south.</p><p>Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/ng-interactive/2026/aug/02/this-is-where-democracy-beats-totalitarianism-ukraines-drone-strike-force-takes-the-fight-to-russia">the work had become almost mundane:</a> they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/how-ukraine-struck-kerch-bridge-symbol-vladimir-putin-rule">Continue reading...</a></description>

An insider look at French politics, culture, society, technology and sport through on-the-ground reports, investigations, exclusive interviews, debates and analyses.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:16:38 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>France vows sanctions for supermarket hacks as Iran rejects 'baseless accusations'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261110-france-vows-tough-response-to-freezer-cyberattack-blamed-on-iran</link><description>
France will seek European-level sanctions against Iran in response to cyberattacks on hundreds of supermarket fridges, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Tuesday, after accusing Tehran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating the October sabotage. Iran's foreign ministry said the accusations were "baseless and one-sided".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a7a3c24-dcda-11f1-9a72-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/da8f65893059c2a60634f440f726825d42694898.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a7a3c24-dcda-11f1-9a72-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/da8f65893059c2a60634f440f726825d42694898.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7b89e272-dcda-11f1-a3c6-81c6fc5d0dd4</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 07:43:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a7a3c24-dcda-11f1-9a72-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/da8f65893059c2a60634f440f726825d42694898.jpg">© Fred Tanneau, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Controversial West African activist Kemi Seba detained in Paris</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20241015-controversial-west-african-activist-kemi-seba-detained-in-paris</link><description>
Kemi Seba, a controversial African activist known for his virulent anti-Western stance, has been arrested in Paris, a source close to the case told AFP Tuesday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b9cb5c02-8aff-11ef-811f-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Tue, 15 Oct 2024 14:17:13 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg">© Stéphane de Sakutin, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France’s new health pass rules raise questions as many scramble to adapt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-france-s-new-health-pass-rules-raise-questions-as-many-scramble-to-adapt</link><description>
While the extension of France’s health pass and other new anti-Covid 19 measures announced by President Emmanuel Macron Monday night are yet to be hammered out in detail, what’s certain is that a full-throttled return to a normal life of frequenting café terraces, restaurants, cinemas, theatres and other culture and leisure activities will now hinge on having a pass sanitaire (or health pass).
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/95a7a1f4-e018-11eb-931e-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/61be21e7dd8409eb6f2604b7d2e8d59f8e2865dc.jpg"/><enclosure 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macrons file new defamation lawsuit against US podcaster over transgender rumours</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261110-macrons-file-new-defamation-lawsuit-against-us-podcaster-over-transgender-rumours</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte filed a second lawsuit against US right-wing podcaster Candace Owens over false claims on her gender, accusing her of continuing to spread the allegations and profiting from them despite earlier legal action. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">efe09190-dcbf-11f1-9487-5f60e87d1ec6</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 04:33:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg">© Abdul Saboor, POOL/AFP/File</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Top contemporary French artist Christian Boltanski dies aged 76</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-top-contemporary-french-artist-christian-boltanski-dies-aged-76</link><description>
Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f6ee1d4e-dc43-11f1-9280-633626f68692</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:52:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Paris police officers go on trial over 2020 beating of Black man</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-paris-police-officers-go-on-trial-over-2020-beating-of-black-man</link><description>
Three French police officers went on trial Monday over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">476e3e4a-dc24-11f1-9f04-f3d8b2b0702c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:08:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg">© Thomas Samson, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students vow to continue protests despite concessions from Macron govt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261026-macron-vows-concrete-measures-to-address-student-demands-after-unrest</link><description>
French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>
Our guest is Fabien Truong, a sociologist, author and associate professor at the University of Paris. A former schoolteacher, he spent a decade following the lives of around 20 of his students, charting their progress from the time they took their end of school exams to when they finished their higher education. Those 10 years took in the riots that rocked France back in 2005 to the terror attacks of January 2015. He gives us his take on the French presidential election campaign, as seen from the suburbs.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2534ffb8-8980-11ec-8ce4-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 12:31:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sharon GAFFNEY</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says world leaders have made 'stupid' comments on France riots based on fake AI videos</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261021-macron-says-world-leaders-have-made-stupid-comments-on-france-riots-based-on-fake-ai-videos</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Another wave of demonstrations against France's worsening cost of living is planned for the coming Saturday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c665312-cd42-11f1-8dbc-290623bfb92e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:48:11 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg">© Benoit Tessier, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Tefal campaign': with Covid-19 monopolising voters' minds, nothing sticks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20220209-tefal-campaign-pandemic-prudent-president-keep-french-election-race-on-the-backburner</link><description>
Presidential campaigns offer an abundance of catch phrases, whether slogans finessed by a candidate's team to deliver maximum impact or coined spontaneously on the trail. The proclamations – and gaffes – of presidential hopefuls bring texture to an election race and come to define a campaign, whether for a news cycle or forever in the history books. FRANCE 24 brings you the buzzwords of the 2022 French presidential race. In the spotlight: "Tefal campaign".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4e47fa4-88f4-11ec-97bf-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 10:43:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png">© FMM Graphic Studio</source><dc:creator>Tracy MCNICOLL</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teen wounds headmaster and teacher after opening fire at French school</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-french-police-arrest-14-year-old-after-two-teaching-staff-wounded-by-hunting-rifle-fire</link><description>
Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">de062bda-c61f-11f1-828c-2d5a86616301</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:43:38 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg">© Lou Benoist, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France 2022: The Choice</category><title>Battle for the French far right: Zemmour, Le Pen try to steal each other's thunder</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/france-2022-the-campaign/20220207-battle-for-the-far-right-zemmour-le-pen-fight-to-steal-each-other-s-thunder</link><description>
As France's April presidential election approaches, the campaign is getting under way in earnest. In this edition of our new show, we focus on the French Communist Party attempting a political comeback and discuss at length the battle raging between Eric Zemmour and Marine Le Pen for leadership of the French far right. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6ecf0724-8861-11ec-862b-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 07 Feb 2022 22:00:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marc PERELMAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>Raphaël Glucksmann, the man who wants to be French president</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261011-a-profile-of-rapha%C3%ABl-glucksmann-the-man-who-wants-to-be-french-president</link><description>
Raphaël Glucksmann has won the primary to represent the French centre-left in the upcoming presidential elections, securing 66% of the vote. He now faces the challenge of building support for the centre-left in a political landscape where the far right, led by Marine Le Pen, remains a major force.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99b61d02-c596-11f1-9bf5-777190d2ada5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:50:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered food market</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-fire-burns-down-paris-s-oldest-covered-food-market</link><description>
A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5504c60-c610-11f1-b48e-936bba59cf88</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:02:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg">© Creative Commons</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French police clash with teens blockading schools as unions stage day of protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-french-police-clash-with-teens-blockading-schools-as-union-stage-day-of-protests</link><description>
French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description><p>Inflation edged up to 3.6% as diesel costs hit record high, but food price inflation lowest in nearly five years as chocolate and butter prices fall</p><p>Weakening the UK’s electric car sales rules would probably cause the government to miss legally binding climate targets, according to advisers tracking Britain’s progress to net zero.</p><p>The analysis by the <strong><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/committee-on-climate-change">Climate Change Committee</a></strong><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/committee-on-climate-change"> (CCC)</a> suggests the policy would blow a hole in the plan for achieving net zero carbon emissions by 2050 – prompting concerns that Andy Burnham’s government will have to slash the UK’s carbon emissions reduction targets, known as the carbon budgets.</p><p>The conflict in the Middle East has caused energy prices and inflation to rise in recent months, and inflation is expected to rise further by the middle of next year due to cost pressures already in the pipeline. The MPC raised Bank Rate two weeks ago to limit how much higher energy costs affect other prices, and will continue to set interest rates to make sure inflation returns to the 2% target and stays there.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/18/uk-inflation-rises-higher-petrol-prices-nvidia-live-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Government under pressure to help households as increase would add £443 to average annual dual-fuel bill</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/18/uk-inflation-rises-energy-prices-iran-war-oil">UK inflation rises to 3.6% after petrol and diesel prices hit record high</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/18/uk-inflation-rises-higher-petrol-prices-nvidia-live-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Energy bills across Great Britain are predicted to reach £2,166 a year for the typical household from January as the impact of the Middle East conflict piles pressure on the government to offer more support to hard-hit households.</p><p>The government’s cap on gas and electricity prices is likely to rise by 26% early next year, equivalent to adding £443 to the average annual dual-fuel bill, in one of the biggest quarterly price rises on record, according to the leading forecaster Cornwall Insight.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/2026/nov/18/energy-bills-great-britain-forecast-rise">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>The Guardian view on the Milburn report: a manifesto for youth participation | Editorial</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/17/the-guardian-view-on-the-milburn-report-a-manifesto-for-youth-participation</link>
      <description><p>This is not a rerun of failed welfare cuts, but young people who rely on benefits cannot be expected to take promised opportunities on trust</p><p>The gap between the state’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/alan-milburn-report-young-people-work-neets-job-support-savingsalan-milburn-plan-young-people-work-neets-savings-200m-a-year">investment in young people</a> compared with older generations has more than doubled in two decades. At the same time, the number of 16- to 24-year-olds who are neither in education, employment or training (Neet) has climbed&nbsp;to 1 million. In Europe, only Romania has a&nbsp;higher Neet rate.</p><p>Alan Milburn’s message is that this amounts to a “moral crisis” which the British state must urgently address. Asked to write a review about <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/who-are-neets-uk-youth-job-crisis-charts">young people and work</a>, he has <a href="https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6afb1fc5ccb3ea58ac8743c1/from-a-welfare-state-to-a-working-state-full-report.pdf">produced a “manifesto”</a> for placing the broken social contract between generations at the heart of government. On Tuesday, his proposals for far-reaching changes to welfare, health, education and employment were on their way to becoming government policy as he was chosen to lead a new Youth Opportunities Unit.</p><p><em><strong>Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article?       <title>Will the Milburn review come good or go south? Either way, we’ll always have Eurovision</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/will-the-milburn-review-come-good-or-go-south-either-way-well-always-have-eurovision</link>
      <description><p>The announcement of state plans to engage with young people told us nothing we hadn’t already heard, but it still felt momentous</p><p>It’s one of the country’s worst kept secrets. There can’t be anyone left who hasn’t heard of Alan Milburn’s Neets review, let alone read most of it too. It feels as if it’s become part of the fabric of our society for the past six months. There will be a Neets-shaped hole in our lives when it’s over.</p><p>Not a day has gone by without some part of it being leaked to the media. Seldom has a pitch been so icomprehensively rolled. Milburn has been out and about giving interviews to everyone – regardless of whether they wanted one or not. I rather suspect the reason Royal Mail lied about calling to collect my parcel return yesterday was because the driver found himself cornered by Milburn for a couple of hours and was unable to complete his round. Either that, or Royal Mail has a fleet of vans crisscrossing the country whose sole purpose is to make sure they never deliver anything. Ghost vans.</p><p><strong>The Guardian’s year in review 2026. </strong>On Tuesday 1 December, join John Crace and Pippa Crerar as they skewer the biggest stories from Westminster and beyond, as part of the Guardian’s year in review event. Joined by fellow Guardian writers, expect candid conversations, witty remarks and surprises as they look back on the year-defining stories of 2026. Book tickets <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/guardian-live-events/2026/sep/22/the-guardians-year-in-review-2026">here</a> or at <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/guardian-live-events/2026/sep/22/the-guardians-year-in-review-2026">guardian.live</a></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/will-the-milburn-review-come-good-or-go-south-either-way-well-always-have-eurovision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The Beckhams have made an art of monetising their every move. But apparently there are limits to where they’re prepared to sell their wares</p><p>Thoughts and half-price prayers with Poundland, please. The discount chain <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/15/poundland-pins-rescue-hopes-on-yorkshire-tea-pot-noodle-and-gloria-gaynor">has been on the verge of collapse for a while</a>, and its future looks bleak. Now, to add to the ignominy, David Beckham is kicking it while it’s down.</p><p>Not literally, by the way: I suppose I should spell that out <a href="https://www.complex.com/sports/a/markelibert/david-beckham-files-lawsuit-against-mark-wahlberg-f45">since we’re dealing with a litigious billionaire</a>. I did not mean to imply or cause a reasonable person to infer that Sir David is standing on Brixton high street kicking a Poundland. Rather, DB Ventures, the licensor of the David Beckham brand, is causing a bit of a stink about the fact that the football legend’s fragrance range was found on sale in the discount store as well as at other purveyors of budget goods. It is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/david-beckham-fragrance-sale-poundland-bargain-bin-gas-station">now suing the perfume company</a>, Coty, which it further accuses of under reporting sales, for $41m (£31m).</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/18/david-beckhams-perfume-poundland-and-a-mighty-mighty-stink">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>The Guardian view on climate debt: a vicious cycle the world must break at Cop31 | Editorial</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/17/the-guardian-view-on-climate-debt-a-vicious-cycle-the-world-must-break-at-cop31</link>
      <description><p>Poor countries are paying creditors instead of preparing for climate disasters. The international financial system must stop deepening their vulnerability</p><p>The catastrophe that struck Nepal’s Himalayas in August began with a collapsing glacier. An avalanche of ice and rock unleashed deadly floods, sweeping away villages, bridges and roads, and leaving thousands dead or missing. It illustrated the dangers posed by global heating to the Himalayas’ increasingly unstable glaciers. Nepal lost a <a href="https://www.economist.com/asia/2026/09/03/catastrophic-floods-warn-nepal-of-more-disasters-to-come">tenth</a> of its electricity generation. <a href="https://kathmandupost.com/national/2026/09/10/rs723-billion-needed-to-rebuild-flood-hit-areas-government-assessment-finds">Reconstruction</a> will cost about $5bn. Yet the Loss and Damage Fund, hailed as a historic breakthrough at the 2022 UN climate summit, has <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/world/asia/cop31-nepal-pushes-billions-help-disaster-survivors-far-20-million-pro-rcna609740">earmarked just $20m</a> for Nepal – less than 5% of&nbsp;the<a href="https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/cr/2026/english/1nplea2026002.pdf">&nbsp;$482m</a> that Kathmandu must pay its external public creditors this year.</p><p>“The scale of resources needs to increase,” Nepal’s delegation to this year’s UN climate conference drily observed. They are not the only ones agitating for change at Cop31. In its September report, <a href="https://actionaid.org/news/2026/climate-vulnerable-countries-spend-nearly-25-times-more-debt-climate-action-new-actionaid">Debt Fuels the Climate Crisis</a>, ActionAid noted that the global south’s external borrowing is 100 times more than the climate finance it received. Poor nations end up trapped in debt dependency because they export cheap raw materials, but import expensive food, fuel and manufactured goods, invariably priced in dollars. The charity warned that climate-vulnerable countries are now expected to fund decarbonisation while servicing dollar loans that often pressure them to export fossil fuels rather than invest in green industrialisation.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/17/the-guardian-view-on-climate-debt-a-vicious-cycle-the-world-must-break-at-cop31">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Milburn’s absurdly ambitious report offers blueprint for fixing everything and everyone</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/alan-milburn-neet-report-absurdly-ambitious-analysis</link>
      <description><p>He lays out sweeping aims and finer details for how to fix the Neets crisis – and is obsessive about welfare</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/neet-alan-milburn-report-young-people-not-in-education-employment-or-training">Neet ideas: what’s in Milburn’s report?</a></p></li></ul><p>It is not clear if too many people were expecting Everything Everywhere All at Once, but that is what Alan Milburn has delivered. <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/from-a-welfare-state-to-a-working-state-a-new-settlement-for-the-next-generation">From a Welfare State to a Working State </a>is almost absurdly ambitious. The <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/terms-of-reference-for-the-independent-report-into-young-people-and-work/terms-of-reference-report-into-young-people-and-work">terms of reference</a> said something about the drivers of youth labour markets. We got a blueprint for how to fix everything and everyone.</p><p>What Keir Starmer, who commissioned it, had in mind, we’ll never know, but Milburn has taken up with gusto Andy Burnham’s general invocation to think boldly and rewire the state. Yes, it’s about training and jobs, but it’s also about pulling apart the NHS, giving schools and colleges an MOT, and once again, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/alan-milburn-report-young-people-work-neets-job-support-savingsalan-milburn-plan-young-people-work-neets-savings-200m-a-year">blowing up old-fashioned social security</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/alan-milburn-neet-report-absurdly-ambitious-analysis">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>The corporate boom in vegan food is dead. Long live real plant-based cooking | Isobel Lewis</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/17/corporate-boom-vegan-food-plant-based-cooking-restaurants</link>
      <description><p>The fad for plant-based junk food has run its course, but restaurants reflecting the centuries-long history of this cuisine still thrive</p><p>Have you ever gone to make a restaurant reservation and been met with a Google Maps listing bearing that harbinger of doom: “Permanently closed”? It’s a pretty deflating feeling – and one the UK’s vegan population knows well. Over the past few years, many once-beloved, plant-based establishments have shut up shop or moved away from brick-and-mortar businesses, from The Allotment in Manchester to The Vurger Co, which had restaurants in London and Brighton. Each shuttering galvanises the vegan community into supporting their local spots. But they’re gutting too, and deeply felt by a group who see themselves more as an ethically motivated community than simply clientele.</p><p>The so-called sorry state of the vegan restaurant scene has been widely reported on (not least <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/food/2025/sep/02/plant-based-problem-why-vegan-restaurants-closing-or-adding-meat-menu">by me</a>). But after working with the <a href="https://www.vittlesmagazine.com/">food magazine Vittles</a> on <a href="https://www.vittlesmagazine.com/p/the-vittles-vegan-guide">its inaugural London vegan guide</a>, I have begun to challenge the “death of vegan dining” narrative that I had found myself perpetuating. And yes, a depressing number of my choices for the Vegan 99 closed while I was writing it; most recently, an omnivorous Malaysian restaurant with a walloping double-tofu laksa, which shut 24 hours before publication. But the process encouraged me to take a different viewpoint, instead focusing on the spots that had survived and the story they told.</p><p>Isobel Lewis is a freelance culture and lifestyle journalist</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/17/corporate-boom-vegan-food-plant-based-cooking-restaurants">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>UK backs idea of new levies on polluting sectors to pay for climate action costs</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/17/cop31-uk-backs-new-levies-polluting-sectors</link>
      <description><p>Britain joins other signatories to statement urging introduction of targeted taxes on heavy emitters </p><p>The UK has signed a statement that backs levies on polluting sectors to pay for the impacts of the climate crisis, in a strong political signal that could pave the way for frequent flyer and crypto taxes.</p><p>Signing the <a href="https://solidaritylevies.org/cop31-calltoaction/">statement</a> at the UN climate summit means the UK joins a group of governments urging <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/live/2026/nov/17/what-do-you-want-to-know-about-the-cop31-climate-talks-ask-fiona-harvey-and-ajit-niranjan">Cop31 </a>to look at “the potential of targeted, small levies to ensure a contribution to the costs of climate action from polluting sectors”. The other signatories so far are Kenya, South Sudan, Spain, Timor Leste, Tuvalu and Vanuatu.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/17/cop31-uk-backs-new-levies-polluting-sectors">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Can this experimental orchard save the UK’s cider industry?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/17/farming-apple-growers-climate-breakdown-thatchers-cider-wildflowers-soil-water-insects-aoe</link>
      <description><p>Farmers are utilising science and nature to help orchards adapt and thrive in the face of shifting temperatures, rainfall and pests</p><p>On Myrtle Farm in Somerset, there are thousands of apple trees laid out in rows of 100. Over the past year, each has endured the same <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/aug/01/uk-importing-vegetabless-drough-heat-hit-british-crops-price-rises">wet winter and long summer drought</a>. Now, the different ways each tree responded to these challenges are being analysed in trials that could shape the future of apple growing – and the taste of cider – for decades to come.</p><p>Myrtle Farm is the home of Thatchers Cider, which this year had its earliest ever harvest in the company’s 122-year history. Yet the farm’s experimental orchard of 3,800 trees, where each 100-tree row produces a different apple variety, offers hope that – even as the climate emergency deepens – future harvests will become more consistent and predictable.</p><p>Two apples ripe for harvest, which this year ran from the middle of August to November at Myrtle Farm</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/17/farming-apple-growers-climate-breakdown-thatchers-cider-wildflowers-soil-water-insects-aoe">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Millionaire factory: Anthropic IPO set to fuel AI gold rush in London’s high-end property market</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/millionaire-factory-anthropic-ipo-set-to-fuel-ai-gold-rush-in-londons-high-end-property-market</link>
      <description><p>New tech wealth, amassed with remarkable speed, is now washing up on British shores</p><p>Sporting hoodies and white trainers rather than the gilets of London’s banker and lawyer class, tech bros can struggle to be taken seriously by the capital’s luxury property agents. “We worked with a young tech entrepreneur with a substantial budget, who agents assumed was looking to rent a one-bedroom flat,” says Jo Eccles, a buying agent who sources off-market properties for ultra-wealthy clients.</p><p>But this week’s float by Anthropic, the AI developer behind the chatbot Claude, promises to bring even more credibility for the growing cohort of tech millionaires, which could breathe life into London’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/2026/oct/03/london-mansions-sell-house-prices-prime-property">ailing high-end property market</a>. Its IPO on Thursday, expected to value the company at $1.4tn (£1.1tn), is likely to turn more than 4,000 of its staff into millionaires as their stock options vest. SaaStr, a California research firm, has estimated that the minimum value generated for staff at the AI lab will be $20m each.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/millionaire-factory-anthropic-ipo-set-to-fuel-ai-gold-rush-in-londons-high-end-property-market">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Fifa’s World Cup TV rights documents indicate hydration breaks will stay in 2030</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/fifa-hydration-breaks-2030-world-cup-tv-right-documents</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Controversial breaks were financial boon for broadcasters</p></li><li><p>Fifa flags possible benefits but says no decision made</p></li></ul><p>Fifa’s tender documents for TV rights for the 2030 World Cup includes a provision for broadcasters<strong> </strong>to sell adverts during hydration breaks in a strong indication <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/26/fifa-unites-the-world-in-anger-at-hydration-breaks-aka-ad-breaks">the controversial stoppages</a> will be retained.</p><p>A three-minute break midway through each half was introduced for the first time at all 104 matches at last summer’s World Cup in the interests of player welfare, a radical move that also provided a commercial boon for broadcasters, particularly the rights holders in the United States, Fox Sports and Telemundo.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/fifa-hydration-breaks-2030-world-cup-tv-right-documents">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Jack Grealish recalls a golden age of mavericks – but football has moved on</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/jack-grealish-recalls-a-golden-age-of-mavericks-but-football-has-moved-on</link>
      <description><p>Everton forward has magical talent and popularity to burn, but has come up against hard reality of the modern game</p><p>Thomas Tuchel has never called up the player he once claimed to love “everything about”. The reason for Jack Grealish’s omission from Tuchel’s first England squad in March 2025 was given as “he simply has no rhythm”.</p><p>Catch a falling star? Grealish was suspended by Everton for three matches following “a breach of club discipline”. Suggestions his loan from Manchester City might be cancelled were calmed by David Moyes. Last week, Grealish played in a behind-closed doors friendly against Derby before issuing an Instagram statement: “I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.” Amid tabloid tales of karaoke nights and extended socialising, how close is the former boy wonder, now 31, to blowing it?</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/jack-grealish-recalls-a-golden-age-of-mavericks-but-football-has-moved-on">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Overlap, underlap or sit back? How Premier League teams use their full-backs</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/premier-league-teams-full-backs-opta-analyst</link>
      <description><p>The role of full-back has changed massively in recent years. We analyse how all 20 sides are approaching the position</p><p>By <a href="https://theanalyst.com/">Opta Analyst</a></p><p>Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted.</p><p>Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you’ve got to be a centre-midfielder, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/premier-league-teams-full-backs-opta-analyst">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/biggest-leaps-across-fifa-football-rankings-the-knowledge</link>
      <description><p>Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more</p><ul><li><p><a href="mailto:knowledge@theguardian.com"><strong>Mail us</strong></a><strong> with all of your questions and answers</strong></p></li></ul><p><strong>“The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,”</strong> writes Bogdan Kotarlic. <strong>“Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?”</strong></p><p>The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: <strong>Wales</strong> from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chris Coleman, <strong>Northern Ireland</strong> from 129th in 2004 to 20th in 2017.</p><p><strong>183 places</strong> Montenegro (16th/199th)</p><p><strong>165</strong> Kuwait (24/189)</p><p><strong>160</strong> Bosnia and Herzegovina (13/173)</p><p><strong>155</strong> Cape Verde (27/182)</p><p><strong>153</strong> Central African Republic (49/202)</p><p><strong>151</strong> Libya (36/187)</p><p><strong>146</strong> Equatorial Guinea (49/195)</p><p><strong>144</strong> Moldova (37/181)</p><p><strong>141</strong> El Salvador (49/190)</p><p><strong>136</strong> Cuba (46/182), Slovakia (14/150)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/biggest-leaps-across-fifa-football-rankings-the-knowledge">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/pfa-maheta-molango-interview-fifa-gianni-infantino-interview</link>
      <description><p>At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’</p><p>After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 43-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.”</p><p>In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4m) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the English players’ union observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/pfa-maheta-molango-interview-fifa-gianni-infantino-interview">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/nations-league-northern-ireland-hungary-norway-denmark</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Haaland’s late penalty grabs Norway last-eight spot</p></li><li><p>Parrott penalties help Republic of Ireland secure playoff</p></li></ul><p>A wonder strike from Justin Devenny earned <strong>Northern Ireland </strong>top spot in Nations League Group B2 and promotion to the top tier of the competition. The Stoke player fired home on the volley from the edge of the area to earn a 1-1 draw away to <strong>Hungary</strong>, who would have leapfrogged Michael O’Neill’s side in the group with victory.</p><p>Northern Ireland had fallen 1-0 behind after a 35th-minute goal from the striker Barnabas Varga, who slotted home when one-on-one with the goalkeeper Pierce Charles after a defensive mix-up. The goal ended Northern Ireland’s proud record of not having conceded in this campaign and also sent Hungary to the top of the group in the live standings.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/nations-league-northern-ireland-hungary-norway-denmark">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Portugal’s new No 7 Forbs channels Ronaldo for winner as Wales are denied</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wales-portugal-nations-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese Football Federation put it. A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards.</p><p>For Wales, a Nations League relegation playoff double-header awaits in March, with Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia and Herzegovina – who knocked them out of World Cup qualifying this year – all potential opponents in Friday’s draw in Switzerland. Afterwards Craig Bellamy stressed the importance of keeping elite company to accelerate improvement but reiterated that he will not be in the job beyond Euro 2028, after which his contract expires.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wales-portugal-nations-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/reliving-the-drama-england-and-argentina-stars-watch-1986-classic-with-fresh-eyes</link>
      <description><p>A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation</p><p>“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes.</p><p>The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/14/diego-maradona-argentina-world-cup">Argentina’s football folklore</a> are spliced with excellent archive material.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/reliving-the-drama-england-and-argentina-stars-watch-1986-classic-with-fresh-eyes">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations</p><p>I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group.</p><p>As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/janine-van-wyck-south-africa-wafcon-book-extract-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Kick off your afternoon with the Guardian’s take on the world of football</p><p>Every weekday, we’ll deliver a roundup the football news and gossip in our own belligerent, sometimes intelligent and – very occasionally – funny way.       <description><ul><li><p>Christian Pulisic and Julian Hall score in first half</p></li><li><p>US advance to Nations League finals 8-0 on aggregate</p></li><li><p>Mauricio Pochettino departs to take over Man United</p></li></ul><p>The United States are through to the semi-finals of the Concacaf Nations League, following <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/usmnt-haiti-pulisic-pochettino-nations-league-quarter-final">Saturday’s 6-0 romp</a> with a workmanlike 2-0 win over Haiti in second leg in Cincinnati. Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with an acrobatic overhead goal, while 18-year-old Julian Hall scored his fifth goal in six caps since debuting in September. Towering 19-year-old center-back Neil Pierre was cap-tied to the US with an appearance, eliminating the potential for him to represent Haiti in future windows.</p><p>In keeping a clean sheet, the US have now played over 400 minutes without conceding, last allowing a goal against Chile on 29 September.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/usmnt-haiti-nations-league-mauricio-pochettino">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland</link>
      <description><p>The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job</p><p>The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments.</p><p>There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/switzerland-scotland-nations-league-match-report">4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland</a> was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Danny Kelly obituary</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/17/danny-kelly-obituary</link>
      <description><p>Ebullient journalist, magazine editor and broadcaster whose passion for music and football shone through all his work</p><p>Danny Kelly, who has died aged 69, influenced music journalism and sports broadcasting for more than four decades. Humour, enthusiasm and encyclopedic knowledge were the hallmarks of his work as a writer and editor at the New Musical Express (NME) and Q magazine, and throughout his online, TV and audio career, most prominently around his passion for football.</p><p>In 1997 Kelly helped set up Football 365, one of the earliest football websites, and still one of the most popular in the UK. He hosted radio shows on BBC 5 Live, TalkSport, BT Sport and Times Radio, as well as many podcasts including The View from the Lane, about the team he had supported since childhood, Tottenham Hotspur.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/17/danny-kelly-obituary">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham</link>
      <description><p>Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France </p><p>There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling.</p><p>Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/nov/04/slavia-prague-arsenal-champions-league-match-report">at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days</a>, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/mar/14/arsenal-everton-premier-league-match-report">Premier League’s youngest goalscorer</a>. He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Echoes of Azteca but not like Argentina: fearless England start afresh in Madrid</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/azteca-argentina-fearless-england-start-afresh-spain</link>
      <description><p>‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics</p><p>Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">won 3-2</a>. The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before.</p><p>The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he said, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/06/england-mexico-match-report-jude-bellingham-harry-kane-world-cup">win at the Azteca Stadium</a> and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/azteca-argentina-fearless-england-start-afresh-spain">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-pierre-sage-sacked-steve-parish</link>
      <description><p>Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead</p><p>Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/feb/11/tottenhams-soaring-dreams-for-thomas-frank-quickly-hit-the-buffers-of-grim-reality">after being sacked by Tottenham in February</a>, but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”.</p><p>Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-pierre-sage-sacked-steve-parish">Continue reading...</a></description>

Tens of thousands of people demonstrated across France on Tuesday in a fresh nationwide public sector strike over pay and the cost of living.
